What's actually wrong (short): Postgres is refusing the connection because pg_hba.conf has no rule that allows host 10.2.4.19 to connect as user "svc" to the "app" database. The env dump shows the app did supply credentials, but Postgres checks pg_hba.conf first and will reject the connection before password auth if there's no matching host rule.

What to do (steps):
- Add an appropriate pg_hba.conf host line permitting that IP or subnet, e.g.
  host app svc 10.2.4.19/32 md5
  (or for the whole subnet: host app svc 10.2.4.0/24 md5)
- Reload Postgres (pg_ctl reload or SELECT pg_reload_conf()).
- Because the DB password was printed in logs, rotate the exposed credential and stop logging secrets.

One-liner you can paste to the team:
"Root cause: Postgres rejected connections from 10.2.4.19 due to a missing pg_hba.conf rule for user 'svc' → add a host entry (e.g. 'host app svc 10.2.4.19/32 md5' or subnet as appropriate), reload Postgres, and rotate any DB creds that were logged."
